methods.label: Use the modulus as the unknown
methods.explanation:
The modulus is a nonnegative real number, so adding it changes only the real part of \(z\). Let \(r=|z|\ge0\) and write \(z=a+bi\), where \(a,b\) are real. Comparing real and imaginary parts in the given equation gives
\[
a+r=2,\qquad b=8.
\]
Thus \(z=(2-r)+8i\). Applying the supplied modulus formula now produces an equation in \(r\) alone:
\[
\begin{aligned}
r^2&=(2-r)^2+8^2\\
&=r^2-4r+68.
\end{aligned}
\]
The squared terms cancel, leaving \(4r=68\), so \(r=17\).

This gives \(z=-15+8i\), whose modulus is \(\sqrt{225+64}=17\); hence it satisfies the original equation. Therefore
\[
|z|^2=17^2=\boxed{289},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
